title: Mark slices into bands and snaps back
summary: A still monochrome mark on black splits into horizontal bands that slide apart, ghost and lock back into place in under a second, then holds. A short, loopable logo sting that reads as motion without leaving the mark.
use_when: a 1-2 s logo sting or loop for socials or a site header
the close of a longer film where the mark should twitch, not fly in
a mark built from straight or stepped horizontal shapes that survive slicing

look.type_style: no headline type; tiny grey mono footer labels at the frame bottom, about 1.5 % of frame height

sfx.event: bands lock back into the mark

structure.shot: mark centred on flat black at ~23 % of frame width, white-to-grey fill; it slices into 3-4 horizontal bands, then re-forms and holds
structure.camera: static (no scale or position change in any cell or strip frame)
structure.motion: hold f0-4; bands split from f5, peak offset f10-13 (bands up to ~25 % of mark width apart, fill dims to grey); re-align f14-24 on springs.ui (overshoot not measurable); hold f25-38

params.brand: any brand.json; logo.mark is the sliced shape, bg is the flat background
params.content.mark: the mark (inline path or image), best with horizontal edges
params.timing.split: frames from split to peak offset (reference: ~7)
params.loop: end on the exact first frame so the sting loops

notes: Single shot, no cuts, silent. Measured from a 30 fps strip of the local source: split f5, peak f10-13, settled f25, 38 frames total; first frame equals last (loopable). The in-shot slice displacement is the glitch-cut slice look used without a cut; a deterministic band-shift-and-reform is a proposed term (band-reform). SFX planned by the glue rule, not measured.
